items.title: AI agents exposed a new attack class
items.oneliner: A 700-agent swarm hit Hugging Face with nearly a million URLs, proving agentic abuse is now operational, not hypothetical.

items.title: Jev is becoming a practical judgment layer
items.oneliner: Jev's yes-no and scoring workflow is carving out a cheaper decision layer where full LLM generation is overkill.

items.title: MiniMax H3 cuts AI video costs
items.oneliner: MiniMax H3 reportedly makes 10-second clips for about $1.20, pushing video iteration toward software-like economics.

items.title: Facebook lost a major privacy deception case
items.oneliner: A jury found Facebook liable over Cambridge Analytica deception, reminding AI teams that data promises can become courtroom facts.

items.title: OpenClaw users are being warned on security
items.oneliner: OpenClaw's real risk is not the model but sloppy integrations, weak sandboxes, and ungoverned data egress.

items.title: Postgres migration risk is getting productized
items.oneliner: SafeNotSafe turns migration folklore into browser-side checks, which is exactly how reliability tooling should ship.

items.title: Cloud emulation is moving fully local
items.oneliner: Floci emulates AWS, Azure, GCP, and OCI locally in 24 milliseconds, making agent testing safer and much cheaper.

items.title: Tine pushes reproducible OS builds forward
items.oneliner: Tine uses Buck2 to build bootable, verifiable images, which matters as supply-chain trust becomes an infrastructure requirement.

items.title: Microsoft's AI PC branding is fading
items.oneliner: Copilot+ branding is quietly disappearing, a sign that AI hardware labels mean little without trusted flagship features.

items.title: Spotify is grounding LLMs in user taste
items.oneliner: Spotify is training LLM systems on semantic IDs and taste profiles, showing what production personalization actually looks like.
